faqs.question: What does the Cytology Reflex to Cell Block and Relevant IHC Body Fluid test measure?
faqs.answer: This test measures the presence of abnormal cells in body fluids, such as pleural fluid, cerebrospinal fluid, ascitic fluid etc.

faqs.question: Why is the Cytology Reflex to Cell Block and Relevant IHC Body Fluid test done?
faqs.answer: This test uses cell blocks and immunohistochemistry (IHC) to detect specific proteins on the surface of abnormal cells. This helps diagnose various diseases. Hence, it is used for the following reasons: • To diagnose cancer: This test helps identify malignant cells in body fluids. • To monitor treatment effectiveness: It assesses the response to cancer treatment. • To diagnose infections: It identifies infectious organisms or abnormal cells related to infections. • To evaluate inflammatory conditions: It can detect abnormal cells associated with inflammation.

faqs.question: When is the Cytology Reflex to Cell Block and Relevant IHC Body Fluid test recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: This test is recommended for individuals who have • Unexplained fluid buildup in the abdomen, chest, or brain. • Suspicion of cancer metastasis or primary tumors in body cavities. • Symptoms suggestive of infections or inflammatory disorders affecting body fluids. • A need for monitoring treatment outcomes in cancer patients.

faqs.question: What if the results of the Cytology Reflex to Cell Block and Relevant IHC Body Fluid test are abnormal?
faqs.answer: Abnormal results may indicate the presence of cancer cells or infectious organisms in the body fluid sample. However, abnormal results do not confirm a diagnosis and need further evaluation.

faqs.question: What to expect during the Cytology Reflex to Cell Block and Relevant IHC Body Fluid test?
faqs.answer: During this test: • You will provide a fluid sample (more than 1 ml) in a leak-proof container. • The sample is sent to the laboratory for analysis.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the Cytology Reflex to Cell Block and Relevant IHC Body Fluid test?
faqs.answer: To prepare for this test: • Collect more than 1 ml of fluid in a leak-proof container, along with relevant clinical details. • Follow any specific instructions given by your doctor regarding fasting or other dietary restrictions. • Bring any relevant CT scan or ultrasound reports that might aid in the interpretation of test results. Please reach out to your healthcare provider for any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with the Cytology Reflex to Cell Block and Relevant IHC Body Fluid test?
faqs.answer: Other tests that may be ordered alongside the Cytology Reflex to Cell Block and Relevant IHC Body Fluid test include: • Flow cytometry: A technique used to analyse cells for specific markers or abnormalities. • Microbiology culture: This determines the presence of infectious organisms in the fluid sample.

faqs.question: What is the Cytology Reflex to Cell Block and Relevant IHC Body Fluid test also known as?
faqs.answer: Body Fluid Cytology with Cell Block and Immunohistochemistry

faqs.question: What is cancer?
faqs.answer: Cancer refers to the uncontrolled growth and spread of abnormal cells in the body. These cells can invade and destroy nearby tissues and organs. Early detection and proper treatment are crucial for managing cancer effectively.
